solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Graduate, spotty, one influencing group adversely (8, two words)

parts.note: Bachelor of Arts, a graduate's degree
dapple can be an adjective meaning marked with spots

explanation.surface: A spotty graduate is accused of leading a whole group astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one rotten fruit spoils the barrel, so the phrase names a person whose bad conduct corrupts the rest.

clue.text: Worthless piano making a booming sound

parts.note: bum as an adjective means worthless or of poor quality
the musical abbreviation for soft, piano

explanation.surface: A dud piano gives out a loud boom.
explanation.definitionFit: Bump is the booming cry of the bittern, a marsh bird, so it names a resonant sound.

clue.text: Mature eyes of old taking in king born out of wedlock?

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the royal letter goes into the old plural

parts.note: eine is an old plural of eye

explanation.surface: Old eyes take in a king of doubtful birth.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into EINE after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulterine means born of adultery, so illegitimate; the question mark admits adultery is one particular way to be born out of wedlock.

clue.text: Thief in a college dividing thing of little value

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the next word, so the pair sits inside it

parts.note: a doit was a tiny old Dutch coin, so a trifle

explanation.surface: A thief in a college causes division over a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacoit is a member of an armed robber gang in India or Burma, so a thief.

clue.text: Gage path to be fashioned where slane is used?

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are formed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A pledge is laid down for shaping a path where a turf tool is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A slane is a spade for cutting turf, and a peat hagg is a working face or pit in a peat bog where it is used.

clue.text: Deposit in mine to behave as specified (6, two words)

indicators.note: in sets the first item inside the second

parts.note: to lay is to set down or deposit

explanation.surface: Placing something in a mine to follow instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To play it (cool, safe, by ear) means to conduct oneself in the stated manner.

clue.text: Judge interrupting liberal primate lost rag

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so the letter goes in the middle

explanation.surface: A judge breaks in on a liberal archbishop who has misplaced his newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: J goes into APE after the P. Primate also means an archbishop, which drives the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapje is a South African word for a rag or cloth; Chambers glosses it as a rag, here a stray one.

clue.text: Lout in Oslo bar knocking back strong drink

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the city and the start of the next word
surface padding for the hidden route, though it also offers a second route on its own

explanation.surface: A yob in a Norwegian pub downing spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed gives a second route too: BOLS, a Dutch liqueur brand (strong drink), knocked back gives the same four letters, so the clue has more than one way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, coarse, uncouth person, close enough in sense to an oafish lout.

clue.text: Former tennis star broke cooker

definitions.meaning: Betty Stöve, Dutch player of the 1970s
past tense of stave, to smash in

explanation.surface: An ex-tennis star went bust and is reduced to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word: a name, a verb in the past tense, and a household item.
explanation.definitionFit: Stove is the Dutch player's surname, the past tense of stave as in staved in, and a cooking range.

clue.text: Ordeal getting lost somewhere in Texas

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: The ordeal of losing one's way in the Lone Star State.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a city in Texas on the Rio Grande, on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Second to none in domineering? Stasi man possibly comes in first

indicators.note: comes in means enters, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Ossi is German slang for an East German, as Stasi agents were

explanation.surface: An East German secret policeman muscles his way to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stasi was the East German secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossiest means most domineering, so the person who outdoes everyone at ordering others about.

clue.text: Provincial governor in trouble restraining impetuousness a little

indicators.note: restraining means holding something in, so one word encloses the following ones

parts.note: élan is dash or impetuous ardour
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A regional governor gets into a bit of hot water through rash behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Élan is borrowed from French and means flair or dash, here stretched to impetuousness; tad is informal for a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: An adelantado was a Spanish official, the military governor of a frontier province, in the age of conquest.

clue.text: With over 1,024 words, it's hardly worth reading

indicators.note: over in a down-or-across clue tells the solver to flip the preceding word, turning it back to front

parts.note: Latin cum means with, as in 'bedroom-cum-study'
in computing K is 1,024 units, here 1,024 words of memory

explanation.surface: A wordy text of over a thousand words is a dull read.
explanation.walkthrough: The binary kilo, 2 to the tenth power, is 1,024, which is why K stands for it here.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is filth or rubbish, used of trashy writing or entertainment that is not worth anyone's time.

clue.text: Relocated Malay Muslims, gloomy away from their base

indicators.note: the base of a word is its final letter, and being away from it means that letter goes

explanation.surface: Displaced Muslim communities are depressed at being far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moros are the Muslim peoples of the southern Philippines, of Malay stock, who settled there from elsewhere in the archipelago.

clue.text: No royalists enjoy life with king entering as No 1 swaggeringly

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this pair goes into the jumbled group
swaggering is a loose, rolling gait, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: NO plus 1 read as the letter I
to live is to enjoy life to the full

explanation.surface: Anti-monarchists live it up as a king swaggers in as top dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliverians were supporters of Oliver Cromwell, Parliament's side in the Civil War, hence opponents of the Royalists.

clue.text: Glühwein left in bedroom container

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, here the short abbreviation inside the vessel

parts.note: a chamber pot, kept in the bedroom

explanation.surface: Someone has left mulled wine in an awkward place in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes between the P and the OTTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotty is a hot spiced drink of wine, much as German Glühwein is mulled wine.

clue.text: They were worthless in having been despatched by spears

indicators.note: despatched means sent away, so the named short word is removed from the longer one

explanation.surface: Worthless fellows were killed with spears, by the sound of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Javel is an old Spenserian word for a rascal or worthless fellow, hence the past tense in the clue.

clue.text: Fuss north of the border, that is after bed is denied to Scottish

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the shortened word, so it comes second
something denied to a word is taken away from it, so those letters are struck out

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
i.e., Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Scot causes a fuss after being refused a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stishie, like stushie, is Scots for an uproar or commotion.

clue.text: It involves men-of-war, each strong, coming into view

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so the pair goes inside the next word

parts.note: F for forte, loud or strong in music

explanation.surface: Warships, all powerful, sail over the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fight is a naval battle, an action between warships, which the old term men-of-war denotes.

clue.text: Inclined to admit as true pass should go inside

indicators.note: going inside means being placed within, so this word sits in the other

parts.note: to grant is to concede that something is so

explanation.surface: Someone is minded to accept that a pass must be moved inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradient as an adjective means sloping or rising by degrees, so tilted or on a slant.

clue.text: Vagrant priest or ragged vicar-poet, one yielding to English

indicators.note: ragged means tattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
yielding to means giving up its place, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Roman numeral one, to be removed

explanation.surface: A tramping cleric, or a scruffy clergyman who writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Patercove is old thieves' cant for a hedge-priest, a wandering, disreputable cleric with no living.

clue.text: Like old-fashioned squire making money in a swindle with crooked earl

indicators.note: in puts one item inside another, the abbreviation going into the fiddle

parts.note: a rig is a trick or swindle
M is an abbreviation for money in economics, as in M1

indicators.note: crooked means bent or dishonest, so the nobleman's letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: An old squire makes his money from a scam with a corrupt nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Armigeral means entitled to bear heraldic arms, the mark of a squire or gentleman in former times.

clue.text: Wild sheep, mother linked with offspring

indicators.note: linked means joined like the rings of a chain, each passing through the other, so the two words interlock

explanation.surface: A ewe out on the hills with her lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words interlock like chain links: MU, then S, then M, then ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Musmon is an old name for the mouflon, a wild sheep of Corsica and Sardinia.

clue.text: Tidy unit, freshly decorated

parts.note: red is a variant spelling of redd, to tidy up

explanation.surface: A neat unit, just painted.
explanation.definitionFit: Redone means done again, so refurbished or redecorated anew.

clue.text: It's maybe in the north, between Shap and Penrith

indicators.note: between means only the stretch lying in the gap between the two places counts, so their outer parts are dropped

parts.note: a village in Cumbria; its first letter is lost
a Cumbrian town; only its opening three letters are kept

explanation.surface: Something might be found on the road from one Cumbrian town to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: Shap and Penrith are towns in Cumbria, northern England; the word straddles the two names, skipping the 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Happen is northern English dialect for perhaps or maybe, as in 'happen it'll rain'.

clue.text: Archaic poem on one round old vase

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the poem goes around the next letter

parts.note: dit is an old word for a ditty or song

explanation.surface: An old poem written about an ancient vase, in the manner of Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes into DIT after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A diota is an ancient two-handled vessel, a kind of jar or vase.

clue.text: Junior fed with mythological tales on Troy in Borders town

indicators.note: fed with means having something put inside, so the short abbreviation takes in the next item

parts.note: the Eddas are the Old Norse collections of myths
T is the abbreviation for troy weight

explanation.surface: A child is raised on Greek legends about Troy in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borders is the Scottish region next to England; Jeddart (more often Jethart) is the local name for Jedburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeddart is a dialect name for Jedburgh, a town in the Scottish Borders region.

clue.text: Climb using clips, end of spring excepted — army regulation

indicators.note: excepted means left out, so the final letter of the leap word is dropped

explanation.surface: An army rule bans climbing with clips except at the end of spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To jumar is to ascend a fixed rope using jumars, clamps that grip the rope, as climbers do.

clue.text: Wearing untidy suit, not having spread (worryingly) (6, two words)

indicators.note: untidy means out of order, so the letters of the outfit are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone in a scruffy suit is told off for not having spread out.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'worryingly' hints at medicine, where a tumour in situ has not spread to other tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ means in its original place, which in oncology describes a cancer still confined to where it began.

clue.text: What'll reverse this rocky upheaval? Rush to help

indicators.note: the solver is asked which word, when written backwards, gives what follows, so the parts are read in the other direction

parts.note: to rip is to rush along headlong

explanation.surface: A question about undoing a geological upheaval, then a call to hurry and assist.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapir is an upward fold in which softer core rock has forced its way through the overlying strata.

clue.text: Year up, Canadian province changes to special winter coat

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the bird that does it, a usage Azed allows

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the letters go backwards

explanation.surface: A year on, someone in Canada switches to a special coat for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rype is the ptarmigan, a grouse whose plumage turns white in winter to match the snow.

clue.text: Assembly in honour of Maggie in recess

indicators.note: a recess is a backward withdrawal, so the pieces retreat and read backwards

parts.note: both are pet forms of Margaret

explanation.surface: A meeting held to honour a woman while Parliament is in recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemot was an Anglo-Saxon assembly or moot, a gathering for legal and public business.

clue.text: Private Eye admits 50% ad lib

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the agent encloses what follows

parts.note: a private eye is a detective, or spy

indicators.note: fifty per cent is half, so only half of the short word is kept

parts.note: the first half of the two-letter word

explanation.surface: The satirical magazine runs an advert that is half improvised.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine. Lib is an old word meaning to castrate or geld.
explanation.definitionFit: To spay is to remove an animal's ovaries, and lib means to geld or neuter, so both name sterilising an animal.

clue.text: Hot on dancing girl in folk party

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a girl dancing at a folk get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal gathering with folk singing and sometimes dancing; this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Opuntia? it might be this, mashed with poi

definitions.text: Opuntia? it might be this, mashed with poi

indicators.note: mashed means crushed together, so the combined letters are mixed up

parts.note: the cactus genus name, read again as the result of the mixing
taken as written; Hawaiian poi is a taro paste

explanation.surface: A cookery puzzle: a prickly pear could be fish mashed with taro paste.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse composite: the answer plus POI, mixed, makes the first word, so taking POI out of its letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a name for the prickly pear, a cactus of the genus Opuntia, as well as the fish.

clue.text: Struggling rep getting stretched put on American show

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so its letters are thrown into a different order

explanation.surface: A floundering sales rep, under strain, puts on a show for American clients.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretense is the US spelling of pretence, a false display or show of something.
